items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: But that's where Lewis used to get off the boat and come catch me playing there all the time to sit in and play with me.

ctx.x: But what about Miss Cole's lawn parties?

That was just at Fing and Willows. Yeah, I played there a couple of times too. And used to have a little place right back of Perdita Street there. A little yard, you know? Yeah. Right there. Perdita and Satova, I think. It was a Franklin. One of them streets. But that's where Lewis used to get off the boat and come catch me playing there all the time to sit in and play with me.
Who ran that place? Was that?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: So Louis Armstrong himself told me I was about as loud a fella that had in New Orleans, 10 times.

ctx.x: What about the volume on the different trumpet players? How loud did they play?

Well, the loudest one you mean honey? Mm-hmm. Well, I don't know, but the teppan they used to yell me at, Ramport and Julian, I played at National Park, that's there in Willow. I don't know how loud I was playing, but they said they could yell me at night. So Louis Armstrong himself told me I was about as loud a fella that had in New Orleans, 10 times. Loud, strong, you know.
Were you as loud as Geppin?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Yeah, I was working with them. Three chumpers, I was in there, Louie and me.

ctx.x: Yeah, I was working with them. Three chumpers, I was in there, Louie and me. Quite a prophet, actually. One of the Zulus had died, huh? One of the Zulus had died. Yeah.
I don't know his name, I didn't know his name. Well, what year would that be about?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1971-04-08
items.q: More than we used to play in the same brass band.

ctx.x: She might put your picture in a magazine. You'll be rich and famous. Yeah, well, no.
More than we used to play in the same brass band.
You didn't know him in Chicago or technical?
